question.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}],{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis of $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ by inspection.
question.worked_solution:
Remember that a basis of $S$ is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans $S.$

From the given vectors, we can see that ${a}_{1}$ is a linear combination of vectors ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
{a}_{1}=1\cdot {a}_{2}+1\cdot {a}_{3}
$$

Consequently, the vector ${a}_{1}$ can be removed from $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ without changing the span. So $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is spanned by just $\{{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$ 

Lastly, note that ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set $\{{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is a linearly independent set that spans $S.$

Therefore, a basis of $S$ is $\{{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\},$ that is to say,

$$
B=\{{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}},{{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}\}.
$$
